Synopsis:
If the player has rescued Omeluum from the Iron Throne, then he is in the Lodge for the Society of Brilliance. He tells the player about the events that led him to be imprisoned on the throne, reflects on the outcomes of the rescue (whether the other hostages/Duke Ravengard were saved), and provides them with a reward for his rescue.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_TheLodge_Omeluum.json: You find Omeluum in the Society of Brilliance’s lodge after rescuing him from the Iron Throne — he was captured while investigating the Foundry/Iron Throne and his work ended in imprisonment. He explains how his inquiry led to his capture, mourns lost colleagues (he names a loyal friend) and expresses disappointment that knowledge and peaceful inquiry were turned toward violence. His reaction to you varies with what happened during the rescue — he will note whether other hostages (including Duke Ravengard) survived or were lost, and may judge you for casualties. Finally, he offers a reward for freeing him; the wider city is tense from Foundry/Steel Watcher activity and the Neurocitor/Control Centre events that framed the rescue.
- IRN_IronThrone_Return.json: Outcome dialog for the Iron throne. Major part with Ravengard thanking the player, explaining that the emperor extended their protection to Ravengard, and that Ravengard will wait for them in camp where they can talk again.
- IRN_IronThrone_ReturnHostages.json: The hostage thanks the player for saving him and/or the other hostages. He will also beg the player to save their families working in the Steelwatch Foundry, giving them the quest if they don't already have it. If the majority of Iron Throne hostages AND the majority of Steelwatch Foundry hostages are saved, they will aid the player by making Steel Watchers on their side for the final battle. Otherwise they won't.Some variation based on whether the player has already been to the Steelwatch foundry and knows about the Iron Throne hostages, promised to help free the Iron Throne hostages, or doesn't know anything about them.If enough Iron Throne hostages survived, they should hint the player that they might reward them if they save their families. If not enough Iron Throne hostages survived, they should make it clear that the player will not receive any signifacant reward, other than narrative and thanks.If EscapedHostage has died, the dialog will trigger by talking to any one of the other surviving Gondians, but a Narrator will talk instead of all of them, as otherwise the permutations are too many. This will be an edge case, as EscapedHostage is very very likely to survive.
- IRN_IronThrone_ReturnRavengard_OM_Wyll_AOM_OOM.json: Outcome dialog for the Iron throne. Wyll gets reunited with Ravengard and they have an OM discussion. Should also explain how Ravengard is now protected by the Emperor's protection and he will be in camp after this.
- IRN_IronThrone_ReturnRavengard_OM_Wyll_COM.json: Outcome dialog for the Iron throne. Wyll gets reunited with Ravengard and they have an OM discussion. Should also explain how Ravengard is now protected by the Emperor's protection and he will be in camp after this.

context: You find Omeluum in the Society of Brilliance’s lodge after rescuing him from the Iron Throne; he explains that his inquiry into the Foundry/Iron Throne led to his capture and imprisonment. He mourns lost colleagues (naming a loyal friend) and is bitter that scholarly work was turned toward violence. Omeluum’s tone and remarks change depending on how the rescue went — he will note whether other Iron Throne hostages (including Duke Ravengard) survived or were lost and may judge you for any casualties, and rescued nobles may be placed under imperial protection and sent to camp. He offers you a reward for freeing him, and the city remains tense from the Foundry/Steel Watcher and Neurocitor/Control Centre events; the fate of the hostages can also influence later support.
